text: [formal, out of breath] Hold — with respect, hold! Do not go into the den, señor — señora — forgive me, I do not know which, and I have run a long way.
after: [formal, out of breath] Wait! Wolves in that den. Give me a moment. I ran all the way from the bend.

text: [straightening] Santiago, squire of the Order of the Dawning Flame. I have been sent to clear these wolves from the road, and I have been sent alone.
after: [straightening] Santiago. I'm a squire with the Order of the Dawning Flame. They sent me to clear this road. No, there's no one else coming.

text: [reddening, honest] Nothing. That is the difficulty. A knight who has done nothing is sent to do something, and a wolf den on a road nobody uses is the something. I will confess to you, as I would to no one in the Order, that I am not certain I can.
after: [reddening, honest] Nothing! This is my first errand. They said the road was quiet. I counted the tracks outside that den twice. Please don't tell the Order I asked for help.

text: [honest] I will confess to you, as I would to no one in the Order, that I am not certain I can. I have never fought anything that was not a straw man.
after: [honest] I've only fought in the training yard. Straw doesn't come at you in a pack. Could you stay?

text: [earnest] An order of knights sworn to the sun and the sunrise: to be first into the dark and last out of it. Our chapter house is far south of here, in the sun-lands, where I was born. The Order sent me north to learn what the roads are like. I am learning.
after: [earnest] Knights sworn to the sun. Our chapter house is down in the sun-lands, where I grew up. I still turn east when I pray, even under all these trees. They sent me north to learn the roads. I hadn't expected to be grateful for strangers this soon.

text: [reddening, then honest] Prayers, mostly. And the sword, and how to stand still while people say unkind things — which, with respect, you are doing very well.
after: [reddening, then honest] Sword practice. Prayers. They didn't put teeth on the practice dummy. With respect, are you going to help?

text: [relieved] God keep you for it. Then I will take the front, because that is what I am for, and you will tell me if I am doing it wrong.
after: [relieved] God keep you. Give me a moment to tighten this strap. All right. Stay behind my shield.

text: [formal, hurt] Of course. God go with you, then. I will — I will manage.
after: [formal, hurt] I see. God go with you. I'll wait until they come out. One at a time, I hope.

text: [uneasy] Burning Gauntlet. A patrol, this far south of the city. They have someone at sword-point — and with respect, by her look, she is not from anywhere near here.
after: [uneasy] Burning Gauntlet. What's a city patrol doing down here? They've got a woman at sword-point. I don't recognise her dress.

text: [formal, tight] A priestess of what, señora? Say it. I would know what I am deciding about.
after: [formal, tight] Which goddess, señora? Tell me her name before I draw my weapon.

text: [quietly] It might. — {target}. Your word decides it. Not mine.
after: [quietly] Yes, it matters to me. {target}, are we stepping in? I'll follow your lead here.

text: [quietly] I cannot ride beside a company that shelters what this one shelters. I have prayed on it, and I have tried to find a way, and I cannot.
after: [quietly] I've prayed over this every night. I still can't accept the company we're keeping. If I stay, we'll have this same argument at every fire. I'm leaving.

text: [formal] If your company changes, you will find me at the Open Hand. I hope it does. I hope that very much. God keep you, {target}.
after: [formal] I'll be at the Open Hand. If you part ways with them, come and find me. I'd like to ride with you again. God keep you, {target}.

text: [low] With respect. You do not have to answer her. She is bargaining.
after: [low] Let her wait. You don't owe her an answer just because she's frightened.

text: [hesitant] The training yard was easy. You knew the other man would stop.
after: [hesitant] In the yard, you could put your hand up and stop the bout. I miss that.

text: [honest] In a real fight, I still want to run. I worry that one day I will.
after: [honest] I pray before we fight. Then I look for somewhere to run. Haven't done it yet. I'm afraid I will.

text: [relieved] Thank you. I needed to hear that from someone who had actually seen me fight.
after: [relieved] Thank you. You've stood beside me. I'll try to remember that when I start worrying again.

text: [easier] I wrote home. Mostly about the people I have met. My mother would worry if I described the fighting.
after: [easier] I wrote to Mother. Told her about you. Left out the fighting, or she'd walk all the way here to fetch me.

text: [fond] She runs a bakery. I used to get up before dawn to carry flour. I complained every morning. Now I miss it.
after: [fond] She has a bakery. I used to carry flour before dawn and complain about the weight. I'd give a good deal to be back there tomorrow morning.

text: [warm] There is a stool by the oven where I used to sleep between deliveries. Mother still keeps it there. She says my room is too far from the work.
after: [warm] She's kept my stool by the oven. I used to sleep there between deliveries. Apparently my bedroom was too far away when she needed another sack.

text: [shy] I would like that too. May we take a little time? I want to know you better.
after: [shy] Yes. I'd like that. Could we take our time? There's still so much I don't know about you.

text: [gentle] Of course. Tell me when you are ready. We can still enjoy each other's company.
after: [gentle] All right. I won't keep asking. Come and sit with me later, if you'd like.

text: [nervous] I enjoy the time we spend together. More than I know how to say properly.
after: [nervous] I've been looking forward to our evenings together. Even when I'm too tired to say much.

text: [earnest] When we have a quiet evening, may I take you to supper? Just the two of us.
after: [earnest] Would you have supper with me when we get a night to ourselves? I'd like to take you somewhere decent.

text: [pleased] Supper, then. I know a decent place. I will try to get through the evening without saluting you.
after: [pleased] Good. I know a place. And if I salute you at the table, please pretend you didn't see it.

text: [bravely] Then I am glad I said it, and I will not say it again. Thank you for hearing it.
after: [bravely] All right. I'm glad you told me plainly. I won't bring it up again.

text: [shouting] For the Dawning Flame! — forgive me. Habit.
after: [shouting] Dawning Flame, keep my hand steady!

text: [earnest] On me! I can take it!
after: [earnest] Get behind my shield! Now!

text: [strained] I am fine! I am — mostly fine!
after: [strained] Caught the mail. I'm standing. Keep going!
